messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: streaming-api p95 SLA breach in eu-west2. Current telemetry: p95=4.2s, p99=12.4s, tail stalls noticed. Alert group: infra/networking @oncall.

alice: seeing the same on dashboards — per-route breakdown shows most of the impact on /v1/streaming/generate (persistent connections). Client retries piling up.

ben: confirmed. Error patterns look like TCP retransmits + TLS handshake retries between AZb -> AZc. Net metrics: outbound retransmit rate +3x, conntrack usage trending up.

carla: customer-facing impact: a large video-transcription customer reported streams freezing and then reconnecting repeatedly. They saw long pauses ~6-10s before new tokens.

dinesh: adding digging notes: running quick top-n on flows, suspected NAT egress path saturation (ephemeral ports) from the worker pool.

alice: can someone run `ss -tan state established | wc -l` and `conntrack -L | wc -l` on a few affected nodes? I can start a tcpdump.

infra-bot: Running quick probes: tcpdump capture initiated on worker-12 (eu-west2-A). Command: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/streaming-stall.pcap -i eth0 port 443 and host 10.20.30.40`

ben: results so far: multiple SYN retransmits and duplicate ACKs in the pcap. TLS handshake completes but often after 2-3 retries from client side. Server side presents no immediate CPU/GPU pressure.

carla: Link to quick flame graphs: https://console.redwood/infradash/streams/4523456780 — shows idle time in network wait state.

alice: I see conntrack close_wait count is high on NAT hosts (worker-egress-3). `conntrack -S` shows ephemeral allocation spike, close_wait backlog. Suspect NAT table exhaustion causing transient connection failures and rehandshakes.

ben: correlating with NAT gateway metrics — transient spike in connections/sec and high ephemeral port usage. Could be a fanout issue: our streaming clients open many keepalive connections which hit ephemeral range when retried.

dinesh: quick mitigation options: 1) increase ephemeral port range and TIME_WAIT recycle on the NAT hosts, 2) failover egress to nat-standby (other AZ), 3) reduce client-side connection churn via 308 routing to dedicated pool.

carla: ops: are we able to shift streaming traffic off the problematic NAT gateway? We need to do a low-risk failover.

ops-oncall: initiating egress reroute runbook now: shifting a small % of traffic to eu-west2-B path (canary) then increase. I'll coordinate with LB team.

incident-bot: Handoff: infra oncall -> ops-oncall. Paging users: @ben, @dinesh for network changes; @alice for observability.

ben: doing a staged egress change: `kubectl apply -f egress-route-canary.yaml` to move 10% of traffic. Monitoring RTT/TLS success and stream stalls.

alice: watching p95 in real-time — after the canary shift, the canary subset p95 dropped to 220ms within 90s. The impacted subset still high.

dinesh: rolling ephemeral port bump on NAT hosts (increase range 32768-61000 -> 32768-65535) + reduced TIME_WAIT via sysctl on nat-standby. Applying to nat-standby first.

infra-bot: NAT metric update: nat-standby ephemeral free ports jumped after change.

carla: customer update draft: "We observed a streaming degradation affecting EU customers; engineers are rerouting traffic and applying network-level fixes. We will share a follow-up once stabilized." Shall I send?

alice: yes send — mention mitigation and no model regressions.

ben: after full reroute to standby and ephemeral bump on main NAT, cluster-wide p95 improved: rolling average p95=280ms, p99=1.1s. Tail stalls mostly resolved.

dinesh: conntrack entries are draining, retransmit rate back to baseline. I still see a few lingering flows in CLOSE_WAIT on worker-egress-3 — cleanup script queued.

ops-oncall: marking incident as mitigated for customer-facing impact. We'll keep it in high watch for 2 hours. Opening follow-up: postmortem + confirmation on autoscaling for NAT egress (capacity + ephemeral port headroom).

carla: assigning postmortem owner: @ben. Please include root cause hypothesis, timeline, mitigations, and recommended permanent fixes (dedicated egress for streaming fleet, limiting client churn, expanding NAT capacity).

incident-bot: Incident severity: Sev2 -> Mitigated. Labels: network, crosszone, nat, streaming, sla.

ben: quick notes to capture: probable chain = client retries -> connection fanout -> NAT ephemeral exhaustion -> increased SYN/TLS retries -> tail stalls -> p95/p99 breach. Will draft full postmortem.

alice: thanks everyone. After-action items: (1) increase default ephemeral ranges in infra baseline, (2) add proactive conntrack alerts, (3) run chaos test to simulate churn, (4) investigate prefix-level egress routing to reduce cross-AZ NAT hops.

ops-oncall: I'll coordinate the follow-ups and schedule a blameless postmortem meeting tomorrow.

carla: closing thread once postmortem link is up. :white_check_mark:
